$comment: P1-28 write-reachability classification (SEC-004), checked by
scripts/ci/check-p1-28-write-reachability.mjs (validate:p1-28-write-reachability).
The OPERATION LIST is not held here. It is derived at check time from the
P1-24 operation register: every apt.* / rec.* operation whose method is not
GET. An operation present in the register and absent here fails as UNWIRED —
that is INT-113, P1-27's dominant defect class, recurring.
REACHABLE requires a real production mutation call site in apps/web/src that
something outside its own module CONSUMES. An adapter nobody imports is a
write nobody can invoke — Wave A landed the whole reception adapter surface
ahead of its screens, so the difference is not theoretical. Tests, comments,
docblocks and the generated lib/api/idempotent-operations.ts do not count and
are excluded by the checker. A path built by a helper (visitPath) counts: the
checker resolves such a helper by shape, not by name.
NOT_YET_WIRED is the day-one allow-list: the phase's frontend waves have not
landed and no screen exists yet. Every entry requires a reason naming the
canonical-plan task that will wire it. The list only SHRINKS: the checker
refuses any NOT_YET_WIRED id that is not on its frozen day-one list, and
refuses an allow-listed operation that IS called — the wave that lands a
screen must flip the entry to REACHABLE in the same change.
DELIBERATELY_ABSENT requires a decisionRef that RESOLVES against the
decisions recorded in canonical-plan.md section 7. Non-emptiness is not
enough: a fabricated reference reads exactly like an approved one, and one
was walked past an earlier version of this gate. The checker now reads the
plan and refuses any reference no decision heading there carries.
Twenty-one operations carry it, all of them the intake-catalogue
management writes PR #227 registered: create, update and status-set across
the seven catalogues. They are absent from apps/web deliberately. The
35-task register is the OPERATOR surface and no canonical P1-28 task binds
a catalogue-administration screen, so who administers these catalogues and
through which surface is an Owner decision that has not been taken. It is
recorded as P1-28-OD-001, and this is the vocabulary's stated purpose: a
future Owner decision recorded AS a decision rather than parked as
not-yet-wired, which the frozen ratchet would refuse anyway.

apt.appointment-create.reason: P1-28-FE-002: the booking screen at /appointments/new submits through the createAppointment adapter.

rec.reception-party-role.reason: P1-28-FE-009: the parties step of the check-in wizard (apps/web/src/features/receptions/components/steps/PartiesStep.tsx) submits through assignPartyRole in apps/web/src/features/receptions/api.ts, which sends POST visitPath(receptionId, '/party-roles'). The gate resolves that helper by shape since the integration wave.

rec.reception-authorization.reason: P1-28-FE-009: the authorization panel of the same parties step (apps/web/src/features/receptions/components/steps/PartiesStep.tsx) submits through recordAuthorization in apps/web/src/features/receptions/api.ts, which sends POST visitPath(receptionId, '/authorizations').

rec.reception-condition-evidence.reason: P1-28-FE-010/011/012/015/016: five condition-evidence wizard steps (apps/web/src/features/receptions/components/steps/{ComplaintsStep,InspectionStep,DamageMapStep,WarningLightsStep,ContentsStep}.tsx) submit through recordConditionEvidence in apps/web/src/features/receptions/api.ts, which sends POST visitPath(receptionId, '/condition-evidence'). All five are registered in apps/web/src/features/receptions/check-in/steps.tsx and rendered by the check-in wizard route. What an OPERATOR can record depends on the tenant's data, and the classification is REACHABLE because four kinds need none of it: complaint, inspection, leak and contents submit on an empty database. Three more are DATA-GATED and their controls appear only once the row they hang off exists — condition_item needs an open inspection (the same step opens one), damage_mark needs a registered damage_map, and warning_light needs a non-empty warning-lamp catalogue, which no operation in this product can populate. damage_map itself is BLOCKED outright: it requires a registered map-template document and the exact version drawn on, both NOT NULL foreign keys of rec.damage_maps into shared.documents / shared.document_versions. This clause used to read 'no operation registers a document', which is false — shared.attachment-upload-authorize is published and creates that row — and the true, stronger reason is that the chain cannot COMPLETE: no document category exists or can be created (so the call fails ERR-RES-001 for every tenant), the default storage provider refuses every signing call, and no version can ever leave pending. The three are recorded as DOCUMENT_CHAIN_BLOCKERS in apps/web/src/features/receptions/media/media-decision.ts and re-derived from the repository by apps/web/tests/p1-28-reception-media.test.ts, so a commit that closes one of them fails a case instead of quietly leaving a stale justification. P1-OD-025 governs whether the chain may exist at all — so damage_mark is unreachable in practice for the same reason, since the map it needs cannot be created here. None of this is stated as 'seven of eight kinds work': apps/web/src/features/receptions/check-in/evidence.ts carries the per-kind coverage table (four wired, three data_gated, one blocked) and every gated or blocked row names the statement the step puts on screen, which tests/reception-evidence.test.ts holds against the step sources in both directions.

rec.reception-signature.reason: Reached by features/receptions/signature-capture.ts, which registers the signature image as a document version, creates the shared.document_links row rec.guard_signature_evidence() requires for the reception_signature category, and then records the reference. It was NOT_YET_WIRED because an operator could produce neither required uuid; the capture chain produces both. rec.signatures stores the reference and never the drawn bytes.

rec.reception-refusal.reason: P1-28-FE-019: the refusal step of the check-in wizard (apps/web/src/features/receptions/components/steps/RefusalStep.tsx) submits through recordRefusal in apps/web/src/features/receptions/api.ts, which sends POST visitPath(receptionId, '/refusals'). It is registered in apps/web/src/features/receptions/check-in/steps.tsx as `reception-refusal` and is distinct from the rec.reception-refuse EXIT command, which this step does not call and says so on screen.

rec.reception-approve.reason: P1-28-FE-020: the decision panel of the summary step (apps/web/src/features/receptions/components/steps/SummaryStep.tsx, registered in apps/web/src/features/receptions/check-in/steps.tsx) submits through approveReception in apps/web/src/features/receptions/api.ts, which sends POST visitPath(receptionId, '/approve') guarded by the If-Match the shell's rec.reception-detail read supplies.

rec.reception-convert-to-work-order.reason: P1-28-FE-022: the conversion step (apps/web/src/features/receptions/components/steps/ConversionStep.tsx, registered in apps/web/src/features/receptions/check-in/steps.tsx) submits through convertReceptionToWorkOrder in apps/web/src/features/receptions/api.ts, which sends POST visitPath(receptionId, '/convert-to-work-order'). A replay answers 200 with alreadyConverted: true and the step renders it as the success it is.

rec.reception-close-without-work.reason: P1-28-FE-020: the 'close without work' form of the summary step (apps/web/src/features/receptions/components/steps/SummaryStep.tsx) submits through closeReceptionWithoutWork in apps/web/src/features/receptions/api.ts, which forwards to closeVisit and sends POST visitPath(receptionId, '/close-without-work'). The gate resolves that path because closeVisit types its tail as a union of string literals, which Waves F/G taught it to enumerate.

rec.reception-refuse.reason: P1-28-FE-020: the 'refuse the visit' form of the same summary step (apps/web/src/features/receptions/components/steps/SummaryStep.tsx) submits through refuseReception in apps/web/src/features/receptions/api.ts, which forwards to closeVisit and sends POST visitPath(receptionId, '/refuse'). This is the terminal EXIT, not rec.reception-refusal, which appends refusal evidence and changes no status.

apt.catalogue-appointment-type-create.reason: Catalogue apt.appointment_types — create. No administration screen exists in this product and no canonical P1-28 task binds one; the capability ships as API only, behind apt.catalogue.manage, which no seed grants to any role. Populating this catalogue is what would unblock FE-002, because appointmentTypeId is a required uuid on apt.appointment-create.

apt.catalogue-appointment-type-update.reason: Catalogue apt.appointment_types — update. Same surface question as the create: an amend needs the same administration screen that has not been decided on, so no apps/web module calls it.

apt.catalogue-appointment-type-status-se.reason: Catalogue apt.appointment_types — status set (retire or restore). Same surface question: the operator surface never withdraws a catalogue row, and the administration surface that would is undecided.

apt.catalogue-cancellation-reason-create.reason: Catalogue apt.cancellation_reasons — create. No administration screen and no canonical task binding one; API only, behind apt.catalogue.manage, granted to no role. Populating this catalogue is what would unblock FE-004, because cancellationReasonId is mandatory on apt.appointment-cancel with no free-text alternative.

apt.catalogue-cancellation-reason-update.reason: Catalogue apt.cancellation_reasons — update. Same surface question as its create; no apps/web module calls it.

apt.catalogue-cancellation-reason-status.reason: Catalogue apt.cancellation_reasons — status set. Same surface question; retiring a reason is an administrative act with no decided surface.

apt.catalogue-source-channel-create.reason: Catalogue apt.source_channels — create. No administration screen and no canonical task binding one; API only, behind apt.catalogue.manage. sourceChannelId is NULLABLE on apt.appointment-create, so an empty channel catalogue degrades FE-002 rather than blocking it — the emptiness is recorded on screen as an absence, not as an error.

apt.catalogue-source-channel-update.reason: Catalogue apt.source_channels — update. Same surface question as its create; no apps/web module calls it.

apt.catalogue-source-channel-status-set.reason: Catalogue apt.source_channels — status set. Same surface question; no apps/web module calls it.

Populating this catalogue answers ONE of FE-014's two blockers; the other is that no operation amends a created visit's fuelLevelId, which is a P1-18 contract gap and not this decision.

rec.catalogue-warning-light-code-create.reason: Catalogue rec.warning_light_codes — create. This is the operation RMC-11 said did not exist; it exists now, and the table is still empty because nothing in the product reaches it. That remaining half is this decision, and it is what keeps FE-015's warning_light evidence kind unusable in the product as shipped.

rec.reception-evidence-binding.reason: Reached by features/receptions/evidence-capture.ts, which binds the exact immutable version it has just registered to one capture requirement. It was DELIBERATELY_ABSENT on the argument that the document chain could not COMPLETE — no category, no storage provider, no version able to leave pending. P1-15 built the chain, the seeds carry seven platform reception_* categories, and the acceptance environment configures a real S3-compatible store, so all three premises are spent.

rec.reception-evidence-binding-finalize.reason: Reached by features/receptions/evidence-capture.ts, which attempts finalization exactly when the registration reports the version ACCEPTED and otherwise returns the bound-but-not-counted state. The old reason turned on acceptance being unreachable by any application role; registerVersionAndScan reads the object back, hashes it and completes the scan, and shared.guard_document_version_transition admits the transition on an exclusively clean verdict.

rec.reception-capture-override.reason: Reached by components/steps/MediaStep.tsx, behind rec.reception.evidence.override and shown only to an operator holding it. The old reason was that waiving a requirement nothing could satisfy would turn an escape hatch into the only path. Capture works now, so the waiver is what it was meant to be: the exception, beside a control that can also be used.

rec.reception-signature-event.reason: Reached by components/steps/SignatureStep.tsx, which offers finalization only against an ACCEPTED version — rec.guard_signature_event() refuses any other — and repudiation, with its mandatory reason, only against a signature that was finalized. The old reason was that neither event could have a subject while no signature could be recorded; signatures are recorded now.

rec.catalogue-damage-map-template-create.reason: Damage-map template administration is a reception configuration catalogue in exactly the sense P1-28-OD-001 raises: no administration screen and no canonical task binding one, API only, behind rec.catalogue.manage, granted to no role. It is additionally blocked by P1-OD-025, because a template revision needs an accepted template document.

rec.catalogue-damage-map-template-versio.reason: Publishing a template revision is the same administration surface as creating the slot, and it needs an ACCEPTED reception_damage_map_template document version, which no application role can produce while P1-OD-025 is open. API only, behind rec.catalogue.manage.

rec.catalogue-damage-map-template-status.reason: Retiring or restoring a template slot is the same administration surface, with the same missing screen. API only, behind rec.catalogue.manage. Bidirectional by design, so no capability is lost by withholding the screen rather than the command.

rec.catalogue-capture-policy-set.reason: The capture policy is a reception configuration catalogue - what a branch requires at intake, and whether a refusal type requires supporting media. Same decision as the twenty-one intake-catalogue writes: no administration screen and no canonical task binding one, API only, behind rec.catalogue.manage, granted to no role. The absence of a rule is the DEFAULT and it is optional, so a tenant that never reaches this endpoint is never blocked by it.
